questions.question: What is the main thing you'll do with the iPhone app? The answer decides what the home screen puts first.

options.label: Triage + reply (Recommended)
options.description: See which sessions are waiting on me, jump in, answer Claude, leave. Waiting sessions get top billing.

options.label: Watch progress
options.description: Mostly glancing at what's running across nodes; input is occasional.

options.label: Full driving
options.description: Long sessions typed from the phone; the terminal is the hero.

questions.question: How should the screens be structured?

options.label: List → push to session (Recommended)
options.description: Native iOS stack: session list is home, tapping pushes a full-screen session, back swipe returns. No drawer.

options.label: Drawer over session
options.description: Session fills the screen; sidebar slides in as a drawer (what the story currently says).

options.label: Show both as variants
options.description: Mock both, with a toggle, and pick after seeing them.

questions.question: What should the terminal on the phone be?

options.label: Read-only xterm + input bar (Recommended)
options.description: Terminal output scrolls freely; a native text field and a key strip (Esc, Tab, arrows, ⌃C, 1/2/3 for choices) sends input.

options.label: Direct-typing xterm
options.description: Tap the terminal to type into it like desktop, with a key strip above the keyboard.

questions.question: Which secondary views should the phone app include?

options.label: Sessions + terminal only
options.description: Keep the phone app tight; everything else stays desktop-only.

options.label: Diff / git changes
options.description: Read-only diff of a session's working tree.

options.label: Backlog item
options.description: View the session's backlog item and plan.

options.label: Launch new session
options.description: Start a session on a repo from the phone.
